messages:
nav: quick thread: telemetry + support shows two tenant reactions to v1 deprecations: some want forced cutover for predictability, others want indefinite slow-extensions. I'm proposing a "grace credits" model surfaced in Console so tenants can spend credits to extend v1 per-route for short windows. Thoughts?

emily: interesting. How would credits be allocated? free trial credits vs paid extensions? We need clear defaults and a CS workflow.

vik: infra note: allowing many extended routes could bloat v1 capacity needs. We must expose per-tenant projected v1 retention % and a global cap, otherwise cluster planning gets impossible.

nav: rough sketch: 
- each tenant gets a one-time free grace allotment (e.g., 30 credits = 30 route-days) on initial deprecation announcement
- credits are consumable: 1 credit = extend one route for one day (configurable)
- tenants can buy credits (monthly pack) via billing UI for larger migrations
- Console shows per-route "grace view": remaining route-days, projected token/cost delta if kept on v1, and a "spend credit" quick action

emily: UX detail: when a tenant spends credits, we should show an expiration modal and add a small audit entry. Also provide a bulk spend modal to extend multiple pinned routes. CS needs CSV export of who spent what and when.

vik: telemetry/ops: add a tenant-level metric v1_grace_active_routes and v1_grace_consumption_rate. Autoscaling should include grace projections when deciding capacity buys. Also need a safety throttle: if global v1 retention > X% we halt new credit purchases until capacity provisioned.

ops-bot: ops-bot: feature flag staged: feature.deprecation.grace_credits.enabled -> targeting canary-ops and staging

nav: backend flags sketch: 
```
feature.deprecation.grace_credits.enabled = boolean
feature.deprecation.grace_credits.free_allotment = integer
feature.deprecation.grace_credits.credit_unit = "route-day"
feature.deprecation.grace_credits.purchase_enabled = boolean
feature.deprecation.grace_credits.global_retention_threshold = 0.2  # pause purchases if >20% retention
```

emily: alert rules: if v1_grace_consumption_rate spikes > 3x baseline or global v1 retained traffic > retention_threshold -> create ops-ticket and surface a console banner: "v1 capacity under stress, purchases paused". Also flag any tenant that uses >50% of free allotment in <48h for CS outreach.

vik: billing: credits purchased must map to recurring invoices. For probes/mirrors we keep them non-billable. But credits should not mask actual token billing; the grace only delays routing to v2. We need a projected-cost-delta widget so tenants see spending credits vs paying for v2 tokens.

nav: good point. Add a per-route "cost vs credit" curve: if keeping on v1 costs more (because of inefficiencies) then that should be clear. Credits are a migration convenience, not a free cost shield.

cs-bot: cs-bot: please include a customer-facing FAQ blurb: how credits work, expiration, refunds, and bulk buy options. Also include a downloadable spend report for exported tickets.

nav: runbook additions: 
- monitor v1_grace_active_routes and v1_grace_consumption_rate dashboards
- if global retention > threshold: disable feature.deprecation.grace_credits.purchase_enabled, notify finance + infra, open capacity provisioning ticket
- if tenant uses >50% free allotment quickly: CS engagement template (email + suggested migration checklist)

emily: UX copy draft for console banner: "v1 deprecation: you have X free grace credits remaining. Spend credits to extend specific routes temporarily or buy additional credits in Billing. Credits are route-days and do not change token billing." Tooltip: "Grace credits let you postpone migrating a route to v2 for a limited time. We still bill tokens normally; credits only delay routing changes."

vik: telemetry fields to add per-tenant: v1_grace_remaining_credits, v1_grace_peak_retention_pct, v1_grace_projected_gpu_seconds_saved (so infra knows potential reduction if tenants migrate).

nav: final governance notes: purchases should be rate-limited per-tenant (e.g., max 500 credits/day) and require fraud checks. Also limit global outstanding credits to a safe cap. I'll open a PR with wireframes, flag contract, and a short canary cohort (start with <50 tenants). Tagging @emily @vik.

emily: thanks. please add a small quick-action in the per-route menu: "Spend 1 credit to extend 1d" with confirm modal showing remaining credits.

nav: will include. PR in ~20m. :thumbsup:
